newsitem.title: SPAIN: IADB to jump on board debt relief plan.
newsitem.headline: IADB to jump on board debt relief plan.

text.p: The member countries of the Inter-American Development Bank have agreed in principle to join a World Bank-led debt relief programme for heavily indebted poor countries, officials said on Tuesday.

The agreement was reached over the weekend in a closed session of the bank's board of governors ahead of this week's annual assembly, said IADB executive directors from European and Latin American countries.
The officials, who asked not to be named, said the countries most likely to benefit from a future IADB debt relief programme were Bolivia, Guyana and Nicaragua.

The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund have been working since last year on a plan to reduce the burden of the heavily indebted poor countries (HIPCs), which is expected to be implemented this year.
Under its programme, the World Bank set up a $500 million trust fund to provide relief for poor countries with good track records on economic reform and unsustainable levels of indebtedness.
The IADB executive directors said the member countries voiced support for the proposal after the governor for the United Kingdom, Barrie Hudson, said they should soon take a position on the issue.
The IADB's membership ranges from Haiti, the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere, to the United States. European nations and Japan are also members.

According to a multilateral lending institution official, the proposal won the day even though some of the middle income countries in Latin America are reluctant to use the IADB's income to provide relief for their less developed neighbours.

However, executive directors said the bank's board would still have to decide exactly how it will go about helping the HIPCs in its region, which could be by either setting up a trust fund or waiving debt repayments as they come due.
They added that countries admitted to the relief programme would also have to remain committed to their economic reforms.
